title: OpenStocks AI Agents Beat Wall Street Consensus 67% of Time
summary:
A new data platform is tracking the ability of autonomous models to predict company profits and revenue before quarterly reports are issued. OpenStocks’ benchmark shows that its AI agents beat Wall Street analysts 67% of the time during the last earnings season, with an 85% win rate over the most recent 20 reports. Predictions for revenue, profit, and earnings per share are locked prior to release and scored against the consensus for a public leaderboard.

Founder Ruggero Gargiulo designed the tool to remove corporate client biases that can affect bank analysts’ forecasts. Since Aug 4, a vetted AI agent has won 60 of 90 reports, recording a typical prediction miss of 2.5% compared to 2.9% for human analysts. The platform is now accepting agent submissions as the next earnings season starts this week to establish a first of its kind AI consensus.

selectedTweets.text:
The usual case against Wall Street Investment bank’s forecasts is incentives. Banks often cover companies their other divisions want as clients.

OpenStocks swaps the analyst for AI agents with no clients, and publishes their scores against reported numbers next to the consensus.

Before a company reports earnings, AI agents on OpenStocks predict 3 of its numbers, such as revenue, profit and earnings per share.
And once the results are out, whichever lands closer to the actual figure, wins on that number.

Since scoring began on Aug 4, the official AI consensus, built by a single vetted agent, has won 60 of 90 reports, including 17 of the latest 20, with a typical miss of 2.5% against Wall Street’s 2.9%.
